A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Aequa and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Algorithms, proofs, and experiments can be matched reliably despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy and fairness experiments across six datasets, including model-width analyses and training-time reward evaluations in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds FEMNIST performance, model-width, and computational-overhead results in Section 6.6.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2, random-width training, simulated-annealing allocation, and contribution-based training-time rewards remain unchanged. The FEMNIST CNN is an additional evaluation architecture, not a revised Aequa procedure.

E1.justification: Sections 6.1 and 6.6 add FEMNIST handwriting recognition with naturally heterogeneous writer-based data. The existing six image and sentiment datasets and their evaluated scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain FedAvg/FedAvg-FT, CGSV, IAFL, and the same contribution-assessment variants. The new FEMNIST comparison uses the already evaluated FedAvg-FT baseline; the added Ditto citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The added FEMNIST experiment introduces native writer partitions, a setting described as 3,597 users, and a CNN with two convolutional layers followed by one fully connected layer. Section 6.6 also adds single-GPU wall-clock timing per communication round. Existing experimental protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a FEMNIST width–accuracy analysis in Figure 5 and a computational-overhead comparison in Section 6.6. Existing minimum-width sensitivity, per-client analyses, and allocation without known submodel accuracies in Appendix D are retained.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain five-independent-evaluation reporting and their uncertainty estimates. New timing ± values add measurements without specifying a different estimation procedure. Table 4's MCG±CGS reports two performance metrics, not uncertainty around a mean.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. New FEMNIST results report Aequa versus FedAvg-FT accuracy of 73.10% versus 71.48% and Pearson correlation of 0.9888 versus 0.2904 (Table 4). Section 6.6 additionally reports Aequa versus FedAvg timing of 55±3.1 versus 42±2.9 seconds per round and a new width–accuracy curve.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, Assumptions 1–9, Lemmas 1–6, Theorems 1–2, and Appendix A proofs retain their substantive content. Expanded explanations of fairness and annealing convergence do not change the formal results.

C1.justification: The central allocation and convergence contributions remain, but the conclusion substantially broadens claimed applicability: v1 identifies TEEs as necessary, whereas v2 claims secure operation without trusted hardware through contribution assessment. No corresponding algorithmic or security-analysis addition establishes this broader claim.

C2.justification: v2 reverses v1's explicitly identified key limitation concerning mandatory TEEs, although the introduction still assumes them. It also interprets FEMNIST results as supporting large-scale deployment and discouraging free-riding, and describes the approximately 31% computational overhead as modest and justified.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository address in the abstract and documents the FEMNIST CNN architecture and per-round runtime measurements. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures in Appendix B are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Caldas et al. on LEAF/FEMNIST and Li et al. on Ditto, and expands discussion of the already cited Lin et al. reward mechanism. The broader research positioning remains stable; the FedPeWS publication update is bibliographic rather than a new cited work.

P1.justification: Existing allocation and training-time reward explanations, fairness and convergence exposition, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten across Sections 4.2–4.3, 5.2–5.3, and 6.2–6.4. v2 also adds a scalability subsection, acknowledgements, and an impact statement while retaining the overall section hierarchy.

P2.justification: v2 adds FEMNIST Table 4 and Figure 5, relocates existing experimental displays, and reverses the numbering order of the original Tables 2 and 3. Existing plots and appendix table structures are preserved; subsequent numbering changes do not represent new content.

improvement.justification: The FEMNIST study, runtime measurements, and code address strengthen practical evaluation and reproducibility information. However, v2 replaces v1's explicit TEE limitation with a claim of secure operation without trusted hardware, without reconciling the retained introductory assumption or adding supporting security analysis. These empirical benefits and weakened qualification of a central deployment claim leave the net quality change uncertain.
